analysis: Reviewed the docs-only PR: docs/developer/test.md (head lines 3 and 173-176) and docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (date stamp, plus the reasoning-control table row near line 1147). The test.md changes bump the date and add two test names (returnedAssistantReasoningRendersLikeReasoningContent, openRouterReasoningContentReturnRequestsAreServed) that describe OpenRouter returned-reasoning tool turns going through the coordinator and local HTTP paths. No runtime code, key handling, attestation, authorization or cache behavior changes, so the threat model assets and boundaries are unaffected in this diff (TB-002, TB-007, T-041 etc. untouched). The protocol-messages.md row documents that GLM5Next prompt policy treats `reasoning: null` and null `reasoning` members as unset, accepts `reasoning.summary` and `reasoning.generate_summary` values auto/concise/detailed as no-ops, and refuses other reasoning members. This describes a stricter or equal input-validation contract, not a relaxation of security. The patch excerpt for protocol-messages.md is truncated, and its full diff and the corresponding provider source (GLM5NextPromptPolicy.swift) were not supplied. I could not verify that the code matches the documentation. Any docs-versus-code drift would be a documentation accuracy matter, not a demonstrated security regression. Remaining integration question: whether the provider implementation actually refuses unknown reasoning members, and whether returned reasoning content in tool turns is handled only inside the E2E-encrypted path. Nothing in the supplied evidence shows plaintext exposure. No findings.
